text: Understanding Git branching is important for teamwork. A branch lets you work on new features without changing the main code. Developers often create a feature branch to add or fix something safely. When the work is finished, they merge it back into the main branch. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This keeps the code clean and reduces mistakes. A good version control workflow means everyone knows where to work and how to combine their changes. With branches, merging, and pull requests, teams can build software together more smoothly and avoid conflicts.
